qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Rockstar's flagship IP (Grand Theft Auto V >200M units sold; Red Dead Redemption) and 2K's licensed NBA 2K sports ecosystem possess rare creative intangibles and high-engagement live-service habits (78.1% of FY2026 net revenue from Recurrent Consumer Spending), yet consolidated economics decisively fail Gate 3b's empirical moat and pricing-power thresholds. First, 5-year median GAAP ROIC (FY2022-FY2026) is deeply negative at -6.74% (+25.8%, -6.74%, -29.1%, -63.6%, -1.62%; v1 10Y avg 6.5%), far below the >=12% hurdle. GAAP operating income has been negative for four consecutive fiscal years (FY2023 -$1,165.2M, FY2024 -$3,590.6M, FY2025 -$4,391.1M, and impairment-free FY2026 -$104.2M); even stripping all goodwill ($1,061.9M) and acquired intangible amortization leaves FY2026 tangible operating ROIC in the mid-single digits (~5-8%) on ~$3.5B-$4.0B of tangible invested capital (including $2,346.3M of capitalized software development costs), failing the >=15% tangible ROIC standard. Second, 5-year incremental ROIIC (FY2021-FY2026) is severely negative: deploying ~$12.7B to acquire Zynga (followed by $5.89B of cumulative goodwill write-downs in FY24-FY25) and scaling capitalized game development produced lower FY2026 EBIT (-$104.2M) and FCF ($461.5M) than pre-deal FY2021 ($629.4M EBIT; $843.4M FCF). Third, consolidated pricing power is structurally constrained: half of revenue (~50.1% mobile) competes in commoditized, ad-arbitrage free-to-play app stores with zero upfront pricing power; console base retail prices moved only once in 15+ years ($60 to $70); and platform gatekeepers (Sony, Microsoft, Apple, Google, Valve) plus sports licensors (NBA/NBPA) siphon 20-30% gross tolls. Primary erosion threats: mobile user-acquisition cost inflation and generative AI/UGC clone competition, platform fee extraction, sports license renewal inflation, and multi-year AAA hit-development execution delays.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (REJECT). While Take-Two owns iconic console franchises (GTA, Red Dead, NBA 2K) serving entrenched daily gaming leisure habits (78.1% FY26 recurrent consumer spending), the consolidated business fails empirical moat verification with a -6.74% 5-year median GAAP ROIC (FY22-FY26), four straight years of GAAP operating losses (including -$104.2M in impairment-free FY2026), deeply negative incremental ROIIC following the value-destructive $12.7B Zynga acquisition ($5.89B goodwill written off; +59% share dilution), and weak net pricing power across its ~50% mobile segment and toll-taking distribution platforms. Not eligible for Calamity Pass: Anchor Gate 4 would independently reject at CAP = 10 (<15Y) due to Tier 3 hit-driven entertainment fade plus Macrotrend #1 AI/UGC mobile content commoditization and Macrotrend #5 exploding $1B+ AAA development cost cycles, and Zynga's permanent capital destruction plus the outsourced ZMC fee model are structural rather than temporary fixable calamities—even accounting for the imminent Nov 19, 2026 GTA VI launch spike. Downstream gates bypassed per waterfall.
qualitative.evidence: Multi-Cycle Financial Record (FY2017-FY2026, March 31 FYE): Revenue scaled from $1,780.0M (FY17), $1,793.3M (FY18), $2,668.0M (FY19), $3,089.3M (FY20), $3,373.2M (FY21), and $3,504.8M (FY22) to $5,349.9M (FY23), $5,349.6M (FY24), $5,633.6M (FY25), and $6,656.4M (FY26, +18.2% YoY) after closing Zynga in May 2022. Gross margin oscillated widely: 42.9% (FY19), 50.1% (FY20), 54.5% (FY21), 56.2% (FY22), 42.7% (FY23), 41.9% (FY24), 54.4% (FY25), and 57.2% (FY26). Operating income peaked pre-Zynga at $629.4M (FY21) and $474.4M (FY22) before turning negative for four consecutive years: -$1,165.2M (FY23), -$3,590.6M (FY24, incl. $2.34B goodwill impairment), -$4,391.1M (FY25, incl. $3.55B goodwill impairment), and -$104.2M (FY26, zero goodwill impairment). GAAP Net Income followed the same collapse: $588.9M (FY21), $418.0M (FY22), -$1,124.7M (FY23), -$3,744.2M (FY24), -$4,478.9M (FY25), and -$298.2M (FY26). GAAP ROIC fell from pre-Zynga ~14-18%+ (Stockrow: 158.2% FY20, 155.2% FY21, 25.8% FY22) to -6.74% (FY23), -29.1% (FY24), -63.6% (FY25), and -1.62% (FY26); v1 10Y avg ROIC was 6.5%. Cash Flow & Software Capitalization: OCF ran $912.3M (FY21) and $258.0M (FY22) before collapsing to $1.1M (FY23), -$16.1M (FY24), and -$45.2M (FY25), rebounding to $624.3M in FY26; FCF (OCF - CapEx) moved from $843.4M (FY21) and $99.4M (FY22) to -$203.1M (FY23), -$157.8M (FY24), -$214.6M (FY25), and $461.5M (FY26). Capitalized software development costs and licenses swelled to $2,346.3M as of Mar 31, 2026 ($2,149.7M for unreleased titles), with -$688.9M (FY26), -$691.6M (FY25), and -$603.4M (FY24) cash outflows for capitalized development vs $412.8M (FY26) amortization/impairment; SBC ran $305.3M (FY26), $324.0M (FY25), and $335.6M (FY24). Segment Mix & 2026-2027 Trajectory: Console/PC/other generated $3,320M (~49.9%) and Mobile/Zynga ~50.1% of FY26 revenue; Recurrent Consumer Spending comprised 78.1% of FY26 revenue (79.4% FY25). In Q2 FY2027 (ended Sept 30, 2026, reported Nov 9, 2026), net bookings fell 18% YoY to $1.60B (missing $1.62B-$1.67B guidance on weaker mobile RCS and NBA 2K27), GAAP revenue was $1.50B (vs $1.77B YoY), and net loss was -$54M (-$0.29/sh). Grand Theft Auto VI was delayed twice (Fall 2025 -> May 26, 2026 -> Nov 19, 2026) and reaffirmed on Nov 9, 2026 for a Nov 19, 2026 console launch, driving FY27 bookings guidance of $8.0B-$8.2B and OCF >$1.0B (~$290M CapEx). M&A, Balance Sheet & Governance: Bought Zynga in May 2022 for ~$12.7B (~$6.2B goodwill), then impaired $5.89B (~95% of Zynga goodwill) across FY24-FY25 while diluting shares ~59% from 116.8M (FY22) to 185.4M (Mar 31, 2026). Executed zero buybacks in FY23-FY26 and issued 4.75M+ shares at $225/sh in May 2025 (~$1.19B proceeds) to retire maturing debt, lowering debt from $4.11B (YE25) to $2.96B (YE26; $151.4M interest expense) and $2.52B at Q2 FY27 ($629.2M ST + $1,890.6M LT) against $1.67B cash & ST investments ($1.15B cash + $524.2M STI) and $3.67B equity. Executive leadership operates via an external management services contract with ZMC Advisors, L.P. (Strauss Zelnick & Karl Slatoff), drawing management fees and $66M-$72M+ peak RCS-linked payouts amid <1% insider equity ownership, routine 10b5-1 sales, workforce restructurings, and ongoing class-action lawsuits over NBA 2K Virtual Currency expiration and randomized loot-box mechanics.
